title: for 语句和 while 语句

text: Repeat with a known count, or until a condition stops you.

init: i = 0 cond: i < n ? body update: i++ true false: exi Loop Use when Shape for the number of steps is known for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) while you stop on a condition while (x > 0) { ... } do … while the body must run at least once do { ... } while (cond);
break leaves the innermost loop at once. continue skips to the next round; in a for the update still runs, in a while it does not, which can loop forever.

title: Pattern: one pass over a stream

text: Many problems need only a few running values, updated once per input: a sum, a count, a minimum, a maximum, the previous value, the current run length. No array is needed when each value is used once.
Running value Start Update sum 0 sum += x count 0 if (ok) cnt++ minimum LLONG_MAX mn = min(mn, x) maximum LLONG_MIN mx = max(mx, x) current run 1 reset to 1 when broken
t t % 10 rev
0 — stop
% 10 takes the last digit, / 10 removes it. Building rev * 10 + digit reverses, and trailing zeros vanish on their own (P1307). Use do … while so that 0 still has one digit.
When the number of steps is unknown, loop with while on the stopping condition and count the rounds. Used for geometric steps (P1423), harmonic sums (P1035) and savings plans (P1089).
Loops inside loops: rows and columns, pairs, tables.

The outer loop picks a row, the inner loop fills it. Write the inner bound in terms of the outer variable to get triangles. A counter that lives outside both loops keeps counting across rows (P5721, P5725).
Reset a per-row counter inside the outer loop, not before it. Total work is the sum of all inner lengths: n rows of up to n items is O(n²).
none

break leaves only the innermost loop. To stop both loops, set a flag and test it in the outer condition (as above), or put the loops in a function and return . Two nested loops over n values cost about n² steps; tighten the bounds (here a * a <= n ) when you can.

title: 循环结构程序设计案例

text: Primes, divisors, brute force with filters, and how fast is fast enough.
not prime 7 7
prime 97 1
If n = a × b with a ≤ b, then a ≤ √n. So testing divisors up to i * i <= n is enough: O(√n) instead of O(n).
Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b), ending when b = 0. C++17 also has gcd(a, b) in the standard library. The smallest factor of n = p × q is p, so the larger is n / p (P1075).

title: Pattern: brute force with a cheap filter first

text: Put the cheap test (palindrome: about 8 steps) before the expensive one (prime: up to √x steps). Most numbers fail the cheap test, so the slow test rarely runs.
Every palindrome with an even number of digits divides by 11, so 11 is the only prime among them. Skipping those ranges makes b up to 108 feasible (P1217).

n up to Allowed complexity Typical shape 108 O(n) one simple loop 105 – 106 O(n log n), O(n√n) at most loop + sqrt test 5000 O(n²) two nested loops 500 O(n³) three nested loops 1012+ O(√n) or O(log n) divisor or digit loop
Rule of thumb: about 108 simple operations per second. Estimate the loop count from the constraints before coding.

Key points to memorise
1. for = known count; while = stop condition; do-while = at least once.
2. break leaves only the innermost loop; use a flag or return to leave several.
3. Running values: sum 0, min LLONG_MAX, max LLONG_MIN, current run 1.
4. Digits: % 10 takes, / 10 removes; copy n first.
5. Prime test to i * i <= n; gcd by Euclid; smallest factor p gives n / p.
6. Nested loops cost the product of their lengths; tighten bounds.
7. Cheap filter before an expensive test; about 108 simple steps per second.
